t: BATTLEFRONT: WWII ROAD TO VICTORY: Battle of Stalingrad
d: German forces encounter Russian resistance.

t: BATTLEFRONT: WWII ROAD TO VICTORY: El Alamein
d: Erwin Rommel battles Allied forces in North Africa in 1942.

t: BATTLEFRONT: WWII ROAD TO VICTORY: North Africa (November 1942)
d: In the North African desert in 1942, American fighting forces encounter the dreaded Rommel for the first time to stop the German war machine.

t: BATTLEFRONT: WWII ROAD TO VICTORY: Burma: The Forgotten Front (Spring 1943)
d: The Japanese meet resistance from British forces as they advance through Burma to take India in 1944.

t: BATTLEFRONT: WWII ROAD TO VICTORY: Battle of Sicily
d: Fresh from victory in North Africa, the Allies successfully invade the island of Sicily, staging an eventual Italian withdrawal from the war.

t: BATTLEFRONT: WWII ROAD TO VICTORY: Bombing of Ploesti
d: American bombers target a Romanian oil refinery in a daring 1943 mission.

t: BATTLEFRONT: WWII ROAD TO VICTORY: Monte Cassino (September 3, 1943)
d: As the allies make their way into Italy, they encounter tremendous resistance at German defensive positions along the Gustav line. One of these locations is an ancient monastery called Monte Cassino.

t: BATTLEFRONT: WWII ROAD TO VICTORY: The Gilbert Islands (November 1943)
d: Bloody fighting erupts on a group of tiny Pacific islands in November 1943.

t: BATTLEFRONT: WWII ROAD TO VICTORY: Battle of Anzio
d: Allied armies encounter German resistance in the Italian fishing town of Anzio.

t: BATTLEFRONT: WWII ROAD TO VICTORY: Kwajalein
d: Examining the battle at the Kwajelein Atoll in the South Pacific during 1944. Included: operations by the Seabees.

t: BATTLEFRONT: WWII ROAD TO VICTORY: Battle in Palau (Summer 1944)
d: As the United States prepared for the invasion of the Philippines, scheduled for late 1944, the tiny Palau Islands had to be taken first.

t: BATTLEFRONT: WWII ROAD TO VICTORY: D-Day (June 6,1944)
d: D-Day, the 6th of June--one of the most pivotal moments in world history. In a massive armada of thousands of ships, 3,000,000 allied troops land at Three Beaches in Normandy, France.

t: BATTLEFRONT: WWII ROAD TO VICTORY: Retaking France
d: Six weeks after the D-Day invasion of the Beaches of Normandy, the allied forces are pushing the Germans back through the French countryside. Town by town is won back as Panzer divisions retreat back to the Meuse River.

t: BATTLEFRONT: WWII ROAD TO VICTORY: Operation Dragoon (August 1944)
d: The Allies break into France and push the Germans back to their own border.

t: BATTLEFRONT: WWII ROAD TO VICTORY: Liberation of the Paris
d: Both political and military expediency were factors in the return of the French capital to its people.

t: BATTLEFRONT: WWII ROAD TO VICTORY: Arnhem
d: The Allies launch an attack designed to push the Germans back to the Rhine River.

t: BATTLEFRONT: WWII ROAD TO VICTORY
d: Gen. Douglas MacArthur's return to the Philippines, and the final push to retake the islands after two years of Japanese occupation.

t: BATTLEFRONT: WWII ROAD TO VICTORY: The Last Stronghold (November 1944)
d: American B-29 high-altitude bomber attacks Japan near the end of World War II.

t: BATTLEFRONT: WWII ROAD TO VICTORY: Mount Belvedere
d: The Battle of the Gothic Line in 1944.

t: BATTLEFRONT: WWII ROAD TO VICTORY: Battle of the Bulge (December 1944)
d: The December 1944 battle pitting American forces against German Panzer divisions in the Ardennes Forest.

t: BATTLEFRONT: WWII ROAD TO VICTORY: Mount Hot Rocks (February 19, 1945)
d: American forces landing on the shores of Iwo Jima encounter Japanese combatants willing to fight to the death.

t: BATTLEFRONT: WWII ROAD TO VICTORY: Battle of Remagen
d: German forces retreat across the Rhine on the Remagen bridge near the close of the war.

t: BATTLEFRONT: WWII ROAD TO VICTORY: Battle of Okinawa
d: Kamikaze pilots guard the island of Okinawa from American forces.

t: BATTLEFRONT: WWII ROAD TO VICTORY: Fall of Berlin
d: In 1945, Soviet and American troops press Hitler's armies from the west and the east, culminating in the fall of Berlin.

t: BATTLEFRONT: WWII ROAD TO VICTORY: Commerce Raiders
d: Heavily armed vessels disguised as ordinary cargo ships patrolled allied waters, sinking supply boats and stealing their content.

t: BATTLEFRONT: WWII ROAD TO VICTORY: Bombing of Germany
d: The development of the B-17 bomber, which allowed American planes to reach inside Germany and bomb its cities.

t: BATTLEFRONT: WWII ROAD TO VICTORY: U-Boat War
d: U-boats posed the deadliest threat to Allied convoys traveling the Atlantic.
